query: Traditional fusion welding can be unsuitable for repairing certain damaged high-value components because their physical and microstructural characteristics create a risk of hot cracking. For preventing or delaying surface-defect initiation, earlier work has used PVD, CVD, electroplating, and thermal diffusion to improve hardness and resistance to wear and corrosion, but these approaches can involve costly deposition equipment, pollution, or long processing times. Under the constraints of avoiding whole-part replacement and limiting these drawbacks, what intervention could repair or improve the surface for service in aggressive environments? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, the operative mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface, its processing and service boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the surface properties and service life of components coated with HEAs to those repaired using traditional fusion welding and untreated surfaces.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEA-coated components do not show significant improvement in surface properties and service life compared to traditional fusion welding and untreated surfaces, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractAlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) films with strong amorphization were obtained by co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition, and the effect of thermal shock on the films was investigated in order to explore the protection mechanism of HEA films against mechanical components in extreme service environments. The results show that after annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing, so that the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film exhibits excellent oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air. In the friction-corrosion coupling environment, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film annealed at 800 °C for 1 h shows the best tribocorrosion resistance due to the stable dense microstructure and excellent mechanical properties, and its ΔOCP, COF and wear rate possess the smallest values of 0.055, 0.04 and 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1.Keywords: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film, thermal shock, oxidation, tribocorrosion
